\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-alternative-small}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale\}$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal{O}_{affine}$-modules
on $S_{affine, \tau}$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every morphism $U \to U'$ of $S_{affine, \tau}$ the map
$\mathcal{F}(U') \otimes_{\mathcal{O}(U')} \mathcal{O}(U) \to \mathcal{F}(U)$
is an isomorphism,
\item $\mathcal{F}$ is a sheaf on $S_{affine, \tau}$ and
a quasi-coherent module on the ringed site
$(S_{affine, \tau}, \mathcal{O}_{affine})$ in the sense of
Modules on Sites, Definition \ref{sites-modules-definition-site-local},
\item $\mathcal{F}$ corresponds to a quasi-coherent module on
$S_\tau$ via the equivalence (\ref{equation-alternative-small-ringed}),
\item $\mathcal{F}$ comes from a unique quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_S$-module $\mathcal{G}$ by the procedure
described in Section \ref{section-quasi-coherent-sheaves}.
\end{enumerate}
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale}\}$. Let $S_{\mathrm{affine},\tau}$ be the full subsite of the small $\tau$-site whose objects are affine open subschemes of $S$ (for Zariski), or affine schemes étale over $S$ (for étale), with standard affine $\tau$-coverings and structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{affine}}(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Its ringed topos is canonically equivalent to the small $\tau$ ringed topos $S_\tau$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathrm{affine}}$-modules on $S_{\mathrm{affine},\tau}$. The following are equivalent: (1) for every morphism $U\to U'$ in that affine subsite, the canonical map $\mathcal F(U')\otimes_{\Gamma(U',\mathcal O_{U'})}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)\to\mathcal F(U)$ is an isomorphism; (2) $\mathcal F$ is a sheaf and a quasi-coherent module on the ringed affine subsite (locally admitting presentations by possibly infinite direct sums of the structure sheaf); (3) under the ringed-topos equivalence from the affine subsite to $S_\tau$, $\mathcal F$ corresponds to a quasi-coherent module on $S_\tau$; (4) there exists a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal G$, unique up to unique isomorphism, with $\mathcal F(U)=\Gamma(U,\mathcal G|_U)$ naturally in every affine object $U\to S$.
hypotheses: tau is small Zariski/étale; F is a presheaf of modules on the affine subsite.
conclusions: Tensor-compatible restriction, site-local quasi-coherence, and descent from unique scheme QCoh are equivalent.
equivalence_sides: For every morphism U→U' in the small affine site, F(U')⊗_(O(U'))O(U)→F(U) is an isomorphism.
F is a sheaf and locally quasi-coherent O-module on S_(affine,τ).
F corresponds to a quasi-coherent module on S_τ under the specified affine-site equivalence.
F arises from a UNIQUE quasi-coherent O_S-module G by the associated-sheaf construction.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-cohomology-parasitic}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\tau \in \{Zar, \etale, smooth,
syntomic, fppf\}$. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a presheaf of
$\mathcal{O}$-modules on $(\Sch/S)_\tau$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{G}$ is parasitic for the $\tau$-topology, then
$H^p_\tau(U, \mathcal{G}) = 0$ for every $U$ open in $S$,
resp.\ \'etale over $S$,
resp.\ smooth over $S$,
resp.\ syntomic over $S$,
resp.\ flat and locally of finite presentation over $S$.
\item If $\mathcal{G}$ is parasitic then $H^p_\tau(U, \mathcal{G}) = 0$
for every $U$ flat over $S$.
\end{enumerate}
statement: Fix a scheme $S$ and $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$. A sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F$ on the big $\tau$-site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is *parasitic* if $\mathcal F(U)=0$ for every object $U\to S$ flat over $S$; it is *parasitic for the $\tau$ topology* if its sections vanish on every member of every $\tau$-covering of $S$. Let $\mathcal G$ be a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules, and interpret $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal G)$ as cohomology of the associated $\tau$-sheaf on the big site over $U$. (1) If $\mathcal G$ is parasitic for the $\tau$-topology, $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $p\geq0$ and every $U\to S$ in the class of $\tau$-objects: open immersions for Zariski, étale morphisms for étale, smooth for smooth, syntomic for syntomic, or flat and locally finitely presented for fppf. (2) If $\mathcal G$ is parasitic, then $H^p_\tau(U,\mathcal G)=0$ for every $p\geq0$ and every morphism $U\to S$ flat over $S$.
hypotheses: G vanishes on tau covering members (part 1) or all S-flat objects (part 2).
conclusions: All site cohomology of G on the indicated classes of objects vanishes.

\label{lemma-direct-image-parasitic}
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. For any parasitic
$\mathcal{O}$-module on $(\Sch/T)_\tau$ the pushforward
$f_*\mathcal{F}$ and the higher direct images $R^if_*\mathcal{F}$
are parasitic $\mathcal{O}$-modules on $(\Sch/S)_\tau$.
statement: Fix a scheme $S$ and $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic},\mathrm{fppf}\}$. A sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F$ on the big $\tau$-site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ is *parasitic* if $\mathcal F(U)=0$ for every object $U\to S$ flat over $S$; it is *parasitic for the $\tau$ topology* if its sections vanish on every member of every $\tau$-covering of $S$. Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and let $\mathcal F$ be a parasitic sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules on the big $\tau$-site of $T$. Then its direct image $f_*\mathcal F$ and every higher direct image $R^if_*\mathcal F$ ($i\geq1$), taken along the induced morphism of big $\tau$-sites, are parasitic as $\mathcal O$-modules on the big $\tau$-site of $S$.
hypotheses: F is parasitic on the big tau site of T and f:T→S is a scheme morphism.
conclusions: Direct and higher direct images remain parasitic on S.

\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-and-flat-base-change}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\tau \in \{Zar, \etale\}$.
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules on
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{G}|_{S_\tau}$ is quasi-coherent, and
\item for every flat, locally finitely presented morphism
$g : U \to S$ the canonical map
$g_{\tau, small}^*(\mathcal{G}|_{S_\tau}) \to \mathcal{G}|_{U_\tau}$
is an isomorphism.
\end{enumerate}
Then $H^p(U, \mathcal{G}) = H^p(U, \mathcal{G}|_{U_\tau})$
for every $U$ flat and locally of finite presentation over $S$.
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme, $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale}\}$, and $\mathcal G$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules on the big fppf site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$. Assume (1) its restriction to the small $\tau$ ringed site $S_\tau$ is quasi-coherent; and (2) for every flat locally finitely presented morphism $g:U\to S$, the canonical comparison map from the small-site pullback $g_{\tau,\mathrm{small}}^*(\mathcal G|_{S_\tau})$ to $\mathcal G|_{U_\tau}$ is an isomorphism. Then for every such $U$ and every $p\geq0$ the natural comparison map from fppf cohomology of $\mathcal G$ over $U$ to cohomology of its restriction on the small site $U_\tau$ is an isomorphism:
$$H^p((\operatorname{Sch}/U)_{\mathrm{fppf}},\mathcal G|_U)\cong H^p(U_\tau,\mathcal G|_{U_\tau}).$$
hypotheses: G big-fppf module; small-site restriction is QCoh and is compatible with small-site pullbacks along all flat locally finitely presented U→S.
conclusions: Big fppf and small tau cohomology agree on these U.

\label{lemma-equiv-fibre-product}
For a scheme $X$ denote $|X|$ the underlying set.
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
Then
$$
|X \times_S X| \to |X| \times_{|S|} |X|
$$
is surjective.
statement: For a morphism of schemes $f:X\to S$, let $|X|$ and $|S|$ denote the sets of topological points. The natural map $|X\times_S X|\to|X|\times_{|S|}|X|$, taking a point of the fibre product to its two projections, is surjective.
hypotheses: f:X→S is any morphism of schemes.
conclusions: Any pair of points of X with the same image in S lifts to a point of X×_S X.

statement:
\label{lemma-universal-effective-epimorphism-affine}
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms of affine schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item for any quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ we have
$$
\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F}) =
\text{Equalizer}\left(
\xymatrix{
\prod\nolimits_{i \in I} \Gamma(X_i, f_i^*\mathcal{F})
\ar@<1ex>[r] \ar@<-1ex>[r] &
\prod\nolimits_{i, j \in I}
\Gamma(X_i \times_X X_j, (f_i \times f_j)^*\mathcal{F})
}
\right)
$$
\item $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ is a universal effective epimorphism
(Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-universal-effective-epimorphisms})
in the category of affine schemes.
\end{enumerate}

Further work needed: The equivalence between the QCoh-section equalizer for any (possibly infinite) affine family and universal effective epimorphism in the *category of affine schemes* depends on the exact test-object and arbitrary affine base-change quantifiers. Its proof invokes the square-zero relative Spec construction and ring-valued functors. Verify the two universal properties are equivalently stated in full, including empty-index and infinite-family conventions, before promoting.
hypotheses: {f_i:X_i→X}_{i∈I} is a family of morphisms of affine schemes.
conclusions: For EVERY quasi-coherent O_X-module F, global sections Γ(X,F) equal the equalizer of ∏_i Γ(X_i,f_i^*F)⇉∏_(i,j)Γ(X_i×_X X_j,(f_i×f_j)^*F).
The family is a universal effective epimorphism in the CATEGORY OF AFFINE schemes.

The family is a universal effective epimorphism in the CATEGORY OF AFFINE schemes.

statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. For any family of scheme maps $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}$, if it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes, then the induced map of underlying topological spaces $\coprod_i|X_i|\to|X|$ is surjective. Likewise, if $X$ and every $X_i$ are affine and the family is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of affine schemes, then $\coprod_i|X_i|\to|X|$ is surjective.
hypotheses: Family is a universal effective epimorphism in schemes, or in affines when all terms affine.
conclusions: The family is jointly surjective on underlying points.

hypotheses: Family universal effective epi in Sch.
conclusions: Disjoint union map surjective.

\label{lemma-check-universal-effective-epimorphism-affine}
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms of schemes.
If for every morphism $Y \to X$ with $Y$ affine the family of base changes
$g_i : Y_i \to Y$ forms an effective epimorphism, then
the family of $f_i$ forms a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes.
statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. Let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a family of morphisms of schemes. Suppose that for every morphism $Y\to X$ with $Y$ an affine scheme, the base-changed family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism in the category of schemes: compatible maps from its members to any test scheme glue uniquely to a map from $Y$. Then the original family is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes (with no affineness restriction on base change $Y\to X$).
hypotheses: All affine base changes of the family are effective epimorphisms of schemes.
conclusions: The family is universally an effective epimorphism in schemes.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-universal-effective-epimorphism}
Let $\{f_i : X_i \to X\}_{i \in I}$ be a family of morphisms of affine
schemes. Assume the equivalent assumption of
Lemma \ref{lemma-universal-effective-epimorphism-affine} hold
and that moreover for any morphism of affines $Y \to X$ the map
$$
\coprod X_i \times_X Y \longrightarrow Y
$$
is a submersive map of topological spaces
(Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-submersive}).
Then our family of morphisms is a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes.
statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. Let $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}$ be a family of morphisms of affine schemes. Assume that for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$, its global sections are the equalizer of the two restriction maps $\prod_i\Gamma(X_i,f_i^*\mathcal F)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\Gamma(X_i\times_X X_j,\mathcal F|_{X_i\times_X X_j})$ (equivalently, the family is a universal effective epimorphism in affine schemes). Assume also that for every affine base change $Y\to X$ the map of topological spaces $\coprod_i|X_i\times_XY|\to|Y|$ is submersive, i.e. surjective and induces the quotient topology on $|Y|$. Then $\{f_i\}$ is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of all schemes.
hypotheses: Affine universal effective epimorphism/equalizer of QCoh sections, plus submersiveness after all affine base changes.
conclusions: The family is a universal effective epimorphism of schemes, not only affines.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms}
Let $\{T_i \to T\}$ be an fpqc covering, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-fpqc-covering}.
Then $\{T_i \to T\}$ is a universal effective epimorphism
in the category of schemes, see
Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-universal-effective-epimorphisms}.
In other words, every representable functor on the category of schemes
satisfies the sheaf condition for the fpqc topology, see
Topologies, Definition \ref{topologies-definition-sheaf-property-fpqc}.
statement: A family $\{f_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ of schemes is a *universal effective epimorphism* (in a specified category of schemes or affine schemes) if, after every base change $Y\to X$ in that category, the induced family $\{X_i\times_XY\to Y\}$ is an effective epimorphism, meaning that for every test object $T$ the sequence $\operatorname{Hom}(Y,T)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_XY,T)\rightrightarrows\prod_{i,j}\operatorname{Hom}(X_i\times_X X_j\times_XY,T)$ is an equalizer. If $\{T_i\to T\}$ is an fpqc covering of a scheme $T$, then it is a universal effective epimorphism in the category of schemes. Equivalently, for every base change $T'\to T$ and every test scheme $Z$, every family of maps $h_i:T_i\times_TT'\to Z$ whose restrictions agree on all pairwise fibre products $(T_i\times_TT')\times_{T'}(T_j\times_TT')$ comes from a unique map $h:T'\to Z$. Thus every representable presheaf $\operatorname{Hom}(-,Z)$ on schemes satisfies fpqc descent.
hypotheses: The family is fpqc, with arbitrary base change and target test scheme.
conclusions: The family is a universally effective epimorphism; representable functors are fpqc sheaves.

\label{lemma-coequalizer-fpqc-local}
Consider schemes $X, Y, Z$ and morphisms $a, b : X \to Y$ and
a morphism $c : Y \to Z$ with $c \circ a = c \circ b$. Set
$d = c \circ a = c \circ b$. If there exists an
fpqc covering $\{Z_i \to Z\}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item for all $i$ the morphism $Y \times_{c, Z} Z_i \to Z_i$
is the coequalizer of $(a, 1) : X \times_{d, Z} Z_i \to Y \times_{c, Z} Z_i$
and $(b, 1) : X \times_{d, Z} Z_i \to Y \times_{c, Z} Z_i$, and
\item for all $i$ and $i'$ the morphism
$Y \times_{c, Z} (Z_i \times_Z Z_{i'}) \to (Z_i \times_Z Z_{i'})$
is the coequalizer of
$(a, 1) : X \times_{d, Z} (Z_i \times_Z Z_{i'}) \to
Y \times_{c, Z} (Z_i \times_Z Z_{i'})$ and
$(b, 1) : X \times_{d, Z} (Z_i \times_Z Z_{i'}) \to
Y \times_{c, Z} (Z_i \times_Z Z_{i'})$
\end{enumerate}
then $c$ is the coequalizer of $a$ and $b$.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-descending-properties}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of schemes.
Let $\tau \in \{fpqc, \linebreak[0] fppf, \linebreak[0]
\etale, \linebreak[0] smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic\}$.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the property is local in the Zariski topology,
\item for any morphism of affine schemes $S' \to S$
which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for $S'$ if property $\mathcal{P}$
holds for $S$, and
\item for any surjective morphism of affine schemes $S' \to S$
which is flat, flat of finite presentation,
\'etale, smooth or syntomic depending on whether $\tau$ is
fpqc, fppf, \'etale, smooth, or syntomic,
property $\mathcal{P}$ holds for $S$ if property $\mathcal{P}$
holds for $S'$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\mathcal{P}$ is $\tau$ local on the base.
statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of schemes and choose $\tau$ among fpqc, fppf, étale, smooth, and syntomic. A property is *local for the $\tau$-topology* if for every $\tau$-covering $\{S_i\to S\}$ it holds on $S$ if and only if it holds on every $S_i$. Suppose (1) $\mathcal P$ is Zariski-local; (2) for every affine morphism $S'\to S$ which is flat (for fpqc), flat of finite presentation (for fppf), étale (for étale), smooth (for smooth), or syntomic (for syntomic), $\mathcal P$ ascends from $S$ to $S'$; and (3) for every surjective affine morphism in the corresponding class, $\mathcal P$ descends from $S'$ to $S$. Then $\mathcal P$ is local for the $\tau$-topology.
hypotheses: P is Zariski-local, ascends through indicated affine tau morphisms, and descends through surjective ones.
conclusions: P can be checked on arbitrary tau coverings.
